Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test org.apache.commons.math.fraction.BigFractionTest.testFloatValueForLargeNumeratorAndDenominator creates a very large BigFraction instance with numerator and denominator having 401 and 400 digits respectively, which results in very large BigInteger values. It then attempts to assert that the floatValue() result is approximately 5.

The bug report states that BigFraction.doubleValue() returns Double.NaN for large numerators or denominators because its implementation simply divides numerator.doubleValue() by denominator.doubleValue(). The problem lies in Java's BigInteger.doubleValue() method, which returns incorrect results (including Infinity or NaN) when the BigInteger is too large (exceeds Double.MAX_VALUE range).

Examining BigFraction.doubleValue() confirms it does exactly that: it directly divides the doubleValue() of numerator and denominator. The same pattern holds for BigFraction.floatValue(). This means that when numerator or denominator BigInteger is very large (like 10^400), their doubleValue() results become unreliable, causing the entire division to fail or produce NaN.

Therefore, the root cause is that the direct usage of numerator.doubleValue() / denominator.doubleValue() is inherently flawed for large BigInteger values, even if the rational value represented by the fraction could still fit in a double or float. A more sophisticated method is needed to safely and accurately convert large BigFraction instances to double or float without relying on BigInteger.doubleValue() which fails beyond a certain magnitude.

Fixing this would require rewriting the doubleValue() and floatValue() methods to handle large numerators and denominators more carefully, possibly by scaling or normalizing the fraction before conversion instead of naïvely dividing two potentially out-of-range doubleValues.

The bug report author suggests they have a patch addressing this problem, indicating it is a known issue and not just a theoretical one.

Hence, the bug occurs because of the implementation of BigFraction.doubleValue() and floatValue() methods that rely on BigInteger.doubleValue() and floatValue() methods that are not reliable for very large BigIntegers.

This matches the test case failure where large numerator and denominator cause floatValue() to fail.

Potentially problematic methods:
- BigFraction.doubleValue()
- BigFraction.floatValue()

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
